blurb: Old Zion German Reformed Church began in the early 1730s when a community of German Reformed farmers met informally in homes and barns. This early group of believers was known as the White Oakland or White Oak congregation. In 1747, the congregation purchased (or received) a three-acre plot of land from Sebastian Reyer (Röyer) and built a log cabin church for worship on this site.
